public_rationale: Hype was high in 2025. Figure raised over $1 billion at a $39 billion valuation in September to build general-purpose humanoids. No Rosie-like robot was released. The most prominent home humanoid, 1X NEO, opened preorders in October for delivery in 2026, and in the WSJ hands-on test all the work was teleoperated by a human. Tesla's Optimus was not released and had production paused over hand-design problems. No source reviewed shows any 2025 humanoid doing a broad range of household chores on its own.
limitations: Rosie is a fictional benchmark, so 'remotely as capable' is judged by plain reading.
Not every 2025 humanoid release worldwide was checked.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In 2025 humanoid robotics will be hyped but no one will release a robot remotely as capable as Rosie; situational awareness and flexibility will remain poor.

statement.excerpt: Humanoid robotics will see a lot of hype, but nobody will release anything to remotely as capable as Rosie the Robot. Motor control may be impressive, but situational awareness and cognitive flexibility will remain poor.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

from_speaker: Humanoid robotics will see a lot of hype
nobody will release anything to remotely as capable as Rosie the Robot
situational awareness and cognitive flexibility will remain poor
where we will be at the end of this year
our_interpretation: Rosie the Robot (The Jetsons) is an autonomous household robot that does general chores and adapts to new situations. Plain reading: by the end of 2025, no company released (made available to buyers) a humanoid that does a broad range of household tasks on its own with flexible situational understanding.
Hype means heavy promotion and investment, such as large funding rounds and bold claims by company leaders.
'Motor control may be impressive' is hedged and not scored.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence of heavy humanoid hype in 2025, and evidence that the leading 2025 humanoids were not released as autonomous general household helpers, for example because they were still teleoperated, delayed, or limited.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A humanoid released to customers in 2025 that autonomously and reliably did a wide range of household chores in ordinary homes, with independent confirmation.

evidence.explanation: A $39 billion valuation for a humanoid startup in 2025 shows the high level of hype and investment the claim predicted.

evidence.explanation: The most prominent 2025 home humanoid, 1X NEO, opened for preorders with delivery in 2026. In the WSJ hands-on test, all the work was done by a remote human operator. That is far from an autonomous Rosie.

evidence.excerpt: Tesla is scaling back plans to produce thousands of Optimus robots this year due to issues with their hand design.
evidence.explanation: Tesla's heavily promoted Optimus was not released in 2025 and had production paused over hand-design problems.
